concomitant gradient effects can cause significant biases in quantitative measurements of T2*, particularly when the T2* of the tissue of interest is similar in magnitude to that of the applied gradient.

the spatially varying magnetic fields that are present in MRI scanners can cause significant spatial biases in T2*-relaxometry measurements that are not accounted for by conventional T2* mapping methods.
